content:
Reportedly, Apple is piloting a new "Live Notes" system at select retail stores. The latest information indicates that the system uses artificial intelligence (AI) technology to record service conversations between Genius Bar staff and customers and convert them into text.

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman mentioned in the latest issue of his "Power On" newsletter that the Live Notes system allows Apple Store employees to "use AI tools to document the service process, transcribe conversations with customers, and organize them into summaries".

The related conversation records will subsequently be stored in Apple's internal Genius Bar system. Bloomberg pointed out that the purpose of this move is to allow employees to focus on handling customer service without being distracted by taking notes.

Reportedly, the Live Notes system requires the consent of both employees and customers before recording can commence at the start of a Genius Bar service.

However, some Apple retail employees have expressed concerns about the potential future uses of the Live Notes system:

Currently, the Live Notes system is not mandatory. Bloomberg pointed out that it remains "unclear" whether Apple will expand the system to more stores, mandate its use by employees, or alter the use of conversation records.
